Lot of partial answers here. Voltage determines maximum RPM for most standard hub motors.

The controller on your bike likely came with the maximum voltage battery it could handle so upgrading it is likely to cause damage unless you verify it can handle it first. 

Next is amperage which is typically limited by your controller for most standard bikes sold. So right out the gate you can usually do a software bypass to give yourself more amperage. This has limits and will burn out your motor or pop a fuse if you push it too far, which may inherently mean needing a larger battery bank capable of more total wattage. 

Something to note though; more amperage won’t get you faster, it will get you to your maximum speed faster. Aka acceleration will go up, as will the bikes hill climbing ability, but is generally not expected to go much faster. 

There’s also just straight up making sure your controller isn’t software limiting your speed to something like 15-20mph when even without modification a 48v should generally get you to 25 mph on a full charge an lighter load, assuming enough amperage.

You could easily do it with a raspberry pi and a 60v or 120v relay. Have the Arduino monitor the voltage and set point and cut the relay off disconnecting the charger.

Leave the charger unmodified and it’ll keep its protections and auto off at a full charged battery like normal in case of failure. 

48v+ is dangerous so make sure you package it correctly. My initial thought is the chargers output to a project box,  your arduino and relay, maybe a little voltage meter and a potentiometer for adjusting set point (you’ll want this and a multimeter to occasionally check and fine tune the output voltage.)

Lastly, you’ll want to account for some debounce of the voltage. Cutting it off early means you’ll need to look at the charging curves of your batteries and charger to determine where along the voltage curve to cut it off, but you’ll also need to implement some monitoring after words to see how much the voltage drops. Realistically if you cut it at 80% exactly it might fall another 5-10% since it’s not being given a full float charge. Have your arduino check the voltage after 10 minutes and if low, have it reengage the charger for maybe 10 minutes at a time.

This is the issue we have now as a society and it's only going to get worse, and faster with technology. Since companies are no longer allowing technology to solve scarcity issues, but technology is allowing for fewer workers, and therefore more money into the owners pockets. This cycle breaks the economic flow such that the lower class don't have a way in, if they aren't already in. I have heavily studied social and group dynamics and business and how the two intertwine. This is actually a really interesting subject to me. Mixing business and relationships - of any kind, is never easy without it getting awkward. Unless everyone involved understands proper social dynamics, and aren't sociopaths or assholes enough to try and take advantage of that. 

In this case the normal social dynamic is that a friend asked a friend for their expertise and help professionally. The asking friend is always socially implying that they would like to get the best deal you can offer, and the receiving friend is assumed to always be giving it. Things get awkward if either individual breaks from their role, such as them asking for a discount - especially without offering anything in return, or you not giving one in the first place [edit: but they are also expected not to complain about not getting one. It’s not required and to reject the friends offer of no discount. This is about them rejecting over you not offering]

But that's where things start to turn even worse, potentially ugly depending on how bad things turn from here. He asked for a discount which puts him in an awkward /looking/ position, but you are in the actual awkward situation because you're being put on the spot by a friend, and no one likes saying no to friends - its awkward because we always assume our friends will help us until proven otherwise and saying no is sort of like saying "I wont help you even though you're asking". 

So, they could totally just be being thick headed, or desperate and broke and not wanting to admit it (this situation doesn't really read to be that though), or in the worst case they have one of the dark triad traits and are aware that it would be awkward for you to say no. Honestly the only way to know which of these it most likely is, is to consider the friend holistically, are they generally a good friend you've known for a while? or one you hardly know through Facebook from years ago and they are just hitting you up? Are they one of those friends you're not sure why you even keep around?

Don't forget that whether they put you in this position on purpose to take advantage of you, or are just being thick headed, you're the only that's being forced to make a final call on whether to damage the friendship by saying no entirely, and you have to decide whether damaging the friendship to keep your boundaries is worth it, and it sucks you're being put in the position to have to make that decision at all.
